 KTAL Shreveport Follow Low voter turnout marked several Caddo Parish races
 Taylor Smith Sun, November 8, 2026 at 9:45 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. SHREVEPORT, La. ( KTAL/KMSS ) — Thousands of Louisiana residents cast ballots in the November 3 election, but turnout figures from several Caddo Parish races show that many registered voters did not participate.
 The election included local contests for mayor, district attorney, judges, school board seats and other public offices.
 Unofficial election results show voter turnout varied across Caddo Parish, with some races drawing fewer than four out of every 10 eligible voters.
In Caddo Parish, reported turnout in several major races included:
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Shreveport mayor: 47% turnout.
 1st Judicial District Attorney: 47.2% turnout.
 Shreveport City Judge, Division D: 37.7% turnout.
 Caddo Parish School Board District 5: 33.5% turnout.
 The figures represent turnout in the specific election districts, not one overall turnout percentage for the entire parish.
 The numbers show that participation differed depending on the race and the area where voters were eligible to cast ballots.
Before Election Day, 520,942 Louisiana voters had already cast early ballots, according to statistics from the Louisiana Secretary of State's Office.
That included:
 448,525 in-person early voters.
 72,417 absentee voters.
 Advertisement Advertisement In Caddo Parish, 24,556 ballots were recorded during the seven-day early voting period.
Those figures represent early voting only and do not include all ballots cast on Election Day.
Before the November 3 election, the Secretary of State's Office projected statewide turnout between 48% and 52% of registered voters.
 For comparison, Louisiana's statewide turnout during previous midterm election cycles was
 2022: 46.7%.
 2018: 50.8%.
 2014: 51.5%.
 The November 2026 statewide figure should be updated once final official turnout statistics are available.
Voter participation determines which candidates take office and which local and statewide issues move forward.
 Advertisement Advertisement Local elections can directly affect decisions involving public safety, schools, infrastructure, taxes and city services.
 The November election included several races that will shape leadership across Northwest Louisiana.
 As election officials finalize the results, turnout statistics will provide a clearer picture of how many registered voters participated and which communities had the highest and lowest participation.
